title: The one dear to me (12.13–12.20)
hook: Krishna ends the chapter on devotion with a portrait, not a ritual
carry: free from hate, friendly to all

segments.voice: Yesterday: the ladder of practice. Fix your mind; if you can't, practice; if you can't, work as offering; if you can't, let go of the fruit. Did you take a smaller rung? Day two hundred three.

There's a kind of friend who doesn't hold grudges. Who's the same at a wedding and a hospital. Who doesn't need anyone to agree with them. People leave their kitchen lighter than they came in, and nobody's quite sure how they do it. Chapter twelve is the chapter of bhakti, devotion. You might expect it to end with instructions: which offering, which mantra, how many times. It doesn't. It ends with a portrait of a person. Eight verses, and a refrain that keeps coming back.
screen: `THE FRIEND WHO HOLDS NO GRUDGES.` → `NOT A RITUAL.` → `A PORTRAIT.`

segments.voice: Verse thirteen opens the portrait. The one who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free of mine and free of ego, the same in pleasure and pain, forgiving. In Sanskrit it starts adveshta sarva-bhutanam: without hatred toward all beings. Then maitra, friendly, and karuna, compassion. And again and again the verses close with some version of the same small phrase: sa me priyah. That one is dear to me. It's Krishna's voice, and it's tender. Verse fifteen turns it both ways. The one from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world. Nobody is afraid of them, and they aren't afraid of anybody. Then the portrait keeps going. Not elated, not hating, not grieving, not craving. The same to friend and enemy, in honor and in insult, in cold and in heat. Quiet. Content with whatever comes. And a surprising word in verse nineteen: aniketa, without a fixed home. Commentators read it as someone who doesn't cling to their house as the center of the universe, not necessarily someone homeless. Notice what isn't on the list. No rank. No caste. No particular ritual. The whole chapter on devotion ends by describing how a devoted person treats everyone else. Verse twenty closes the chapter: those who follow this with faith are exceedingly dear. That's the word today: the one dear to me. And that closes the chapter, and the week. We started with the vision that shook Arjuna, and we end with a kind face.
screen: `HATING NO BEING.` · `NO ONE AFRAID OF THEM.` · `THE SAME IN HONOR AND INSULT.` · `THAT ONE IS DEAR TO ME.` · then, large: `THE ONE DEAR TO ME.`

segments.voice: Sit, and recall one recent moment of praise and one recent moment of criticism. A compliment, a sharp word. Hold the praise for a breath, and notice what happens in you. Hold the criticism for a breath, and notice that too. Then see if, for a few breaths, you can let both sit side by side: the same in honor and insult, as verse eighteen puts it. You don't have to feel nothing. Just stay even. The bell holds the time.
The one dear to me. Gita twelve, thirteen to twenty: a portrait of the devoted person, free of hate, friendly and kind, and the refrain, that one is dear to me.
screen: `THE ONE DEAR TO ME — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: free from hate, friendly to all. That's the week: the vision in chapter eleven, form or formless, the ladder, and the portrait. Today, let one person leave you lighter than they came. Day two hundred three.

howItsDone: Gita chapter twelve, the chapter of bhakti, is short, and many Hindus memorize or recite it; its closing verses (12.13–12.20) are often read as a description of the devotee's character.

fork.setup: you've reached the end of the chapter on devotion. what does Krishna finish with?
options: the right offerings and their times.
a portrait of how the devoted person treats everyone.
a warning to those who don't worship.
fork.reveal: a portrait. eight verses on character, with the refrain 'that one is dear to me' coming back again and again.

original.note: Sanskrit: priya, dear, beloved; the refrain 'sa me priyah', that one is dear to me.

trapdoor: what you thought: devotion means how much worship you do.
what it means: in Gita 12 devotion ends in character: free of hate, friendly, the same in praise and insult.
what a scholar hears: 12.13 opens 'adveshta sarva-bhutanam maitrah karuna eva ca'; the refrain 'sa me priyah' recurs through 12.20.
